question: What does the field of Human-Computer Interaction primarily study?

options.A: The chemical composition of medical equipment materials
options.B: Hospital architectural layouts and structural engineering
options.D: How humans interact with digital systems and technology

explanation: HCI focuses specifically on the ways users interface with software and hardware tools to accomplish tasks. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is Human-Computer Interaction particularly vital for the nursing profession?

options.A: Nurses are the primary users of most hospital digital technologies
options.B: Hospital computers eliminate the need for interprofessional communication
options.C: Clinical software replaces all direct physical patient assessments
options.D: Nurses are legally required to write computer programming code

explanation: Because nursing staff utilize clinical technology more frequently than almost any other group, poor software design heavily impacts their daily workflow and patient safety. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of user-centered design in clinical software?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any staff training sessions or manuals
options.B: Ensuring systems align with the actual workflows and needs of users
options.C: Maximizing the amount of data stored on external cloud servers
options.D: Minimizing the overall financial cost of computer hardware purchases

explanation: User-centered design prioritizes the habits, tasks, and cognitive needs of the people actually using the tool. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which design principle is demonstrated when an interface uses familiar clinical terminology rather than obscure computer programming codes?

options.B: Match between system and the real world

explanation: Using clinical language that mirrors real-world nursing practice helps users understand and navigate software naturally. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which interface modality is most commonly found on standard hospital desktop workstations and computer monitors?
explanation: GUIs utilize visual elements like windows, icons, and menus to facilitate user interaction on standard screens. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h3)

question: In which clinical scenario would a voice-recognition interface be most beneficial to a nurse?

options.A: Typing a lengthy annual performance review in the human resources portal
options.B: Dictating sterile dressing change observations while wearing gloves
options.C: Reading historical discharge summaries from a paper archive room
options.D: Calculating complex medication drip dosages on a calculator app

explanation: Voice input allows hands-free data entry, which is especially useful when physical touch of a keyboard or mouse is restricted by sterility. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is cognitive load in the context of clinical technology use?

options.A: The speed at which a computer processor executes background code
options.B: The total storage capacity of hospital server hard drives
options.C: The physical weight of mobile computer carts used during rounds
options.D: The amount of mental processing power required to use an interface

explanation: Cognitive load refers to the demand placed on human working memory while performing tasks like navigating software. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h4)

question: A nurse is using a poorly designed EHR with cluttered screens and hidden menus during a busy shift. What is the most likely clinical consequence of this high cognitive load?

options.A: Enhanced ability to multitask without missing any subtle patient changes
options.B: Increased risk of oversight and documentation errors due to mental fatigue
options.C: Complete elimination of all communication delays between departments
options.D: Immediate physical injury from repetitive strain on wrist muscles

explanation: When software demands excessive mental effort to navigate, working memory becomes overloaded, raising the likelihood of mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h4)

question: What does usability testing typically involve in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Surveying hospital patients about their billing statement accuracy
options.B: Disassembling computer hardware components to test electrical wiring
options.C: Calculating the financial return on investment for software purchases
options.D: Observing real clinicians performing standard tasks on the software

explanation: Usability testing watches actual users interact with the system to identify workflow friction and design flaws. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical metric measured during formal EHR usability testing?

options.A: Physical height of the desk supporting the monitor
options.B: Subjective user satisfaction scores reported after the test
options.C: Number of mouse clicks or screen taps needed to place an order
options.D: Total time required to complete a specific documentation task

explanation: Usability testing focuses on software interaction metrics like time, clicks, and satisfaction rather than office furniture dimensions. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: What phenomenon occurs when clinicians become desensitized due to an excessive volume of pop-up warnings?
explanation: Constant low-priority warnings lead users to ignore or quickly dismiss all alerts, including critical safety notifications. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)

question: How can software developers best address the problem of alert fatigue in hospital information systems?

options.A: Removing all warning notifications entirely from the software platform
options.B: Increasing the brightness and flashing speed of every warning message
options.C: Calibrating alerts to trigger only for clinically significant and urgent events
options.D: Requiring a supervisor password override for every single pop-up box

explanation: Limiting interrupts to true clinical emergencies prevents users from being overwhelmed and restores the impact of safety warnings. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why is frontline nurse participation essential during the development of clinical software?

options.A: Nurses are legally required to sign off on software copyright licenses
options.B: Clinical staff handle the financial budgeting for hospital IT upgrades
options.C: Hospital accreditation standards prohibit IT teams from working alone
options.D: Engineers need insight into actual bedside workflows and clinical logic

explanation: Frontline nurses bridge the gap between technical software design and the practical realities of patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary function of a nurse informaticist within a healthcare technology team?

options.A: Translating clinical needs into system design requirements for IT developers
options.B: Managing hospital financial accounts and purchasing software licenses
options.C: Conducting direct bedside nursing care for intensive care patients
options.D: Repairing broken computer hardware components and replacing power supplies

explanation: Nurse informaticists combine clinical expertise with technology knowledge to ensure systems support safe, efficient patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which emerging technology streams continuous physiological patient data into records without manual entry?
explanation: Wearables and smart patches automatically monitor and transmit vital signs directly to digital health systems. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h8)

question: How do augmented reality tools change the way clinicians interact with patient data during procedures?

options.A: By restricting software access exclusively to hospital administrative offices
options.B: By projecting digital information directly into the clinician's physical field of view
options.C: By eliminating the need for any vital sign assessment or physical touch
options.D: By replacing all patient monitoring equipment with standard paper charts

explanation: AR overlays digital data like anatomical guides into the physical workspace, allowing hands-free visual reference during care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h8)
